So that's the finer point of my post. Income tax receipts don't go to fund Social Security at all. Paying federal taxes goes two places:

1) The FICA line on your paystub which is a flat 7.65% of your income. This money goes straight to the Trust Funds for OASDI (Social Security) and Medicare Part A. The Congress can't do anything with this money - it's kept separate from the General Fund

2) Income tax (what you fill out the 1040 for every year) money goes into the General Fund and pays for everything else. Medicare Parts B and D, Defense, NASA, Intel, HHS, Congressional salaries, etc. This is the money Congress is allowed to argue over each year. The first (low amount...whatever the standard deduction is this year) isn't taxed at all. Above that, it's 10% for ABOUT $10K and every increment above that is taxed at a higher and higher rate until you hit the max (~40% for all income over ~$400k). See this link for an example of how that works. Remember you only pay tax on your taxable income - the amount left over after all your deductions (and everything you've been able to shelter or hide if you're filthy rich).
